changes: Ratings changes: the NBA column shows team names (76ers, Bucks, Cavaliers) instead of abbreviations
Ratings changes: a new NBA column shows the real team 2K lists each player on. It starts with today's update; older changes show a dash
Free agency: an in-season minimum offer now shows what Year 1 comes to if signed today. The deal is prorated on the day it goes through, so the offer keeps the full-season figure
Rulebook § 3.12: in-season minimum signings are now written at the prorated figure automatically
Player pages: the stats tables run oldest season first, with a traded season's teams in the order he played for them and each season's playoffs right after it
Coaching tab: positions are one button per player. Tap it to keep his positions or take 2K's new ones, pick a secondary, and have the streamer check them before every game, all in one labelled panel
The read view marks a player 2K has re-rated with a short "2K changed" tag; his team can tap it to open that panel
Coaching tab: when 2K has changed a player's positions, the tag now reads "2K now: PF/SF", and your front office can tap it to take 2K's positions (you still press Save)
Power rankings ballot: every team shows its record, seed, last 10, streak, point differential and last edition's rank right on the row, so you can rank without opening anything
Tap a team for its roster with this season's averages (starters first), its last five games, injuries, playoff odds and the model's rank. Open all opens every team at once
Reordering works on a phone: drag a team by its handle, or tap its rank and type a new one. Start your ballot from last edition, the standings or the model rating
Blurbs: the team's roster and recent games sit beside the box while you write, every team shows its record, and Your teams jumps straight to the teams you claimed
The consensus table fits a phone: the average and high/low fold under the team name
Homepage: the Utah Jazz logo shows on the your-team band and the Quick Links card (it was white on a white circle)
The homepage Quick Links card is redesigned in your team's colours: a banner for your team with its logo and its secondary mark, then Coaching and Betting tiles. Betting shows your NB¥ balance

Quick links are now their own card on the homepage, at the top of the right-hand column: Coaching Settings, your team and Betting. They are no longer in the top-right corner of every page. Signed out, the card doesn't show
Signed-in members get Quick links at the top right of every page: Coaching settings, your team page and Betting. Signed out, there are none
Search (Ctrl+K) finds Coaching (also "lineup", "rotation", "minutes"), which opens your own team's Coaching tab

Team pages: draft picks read cleanly on a phone. Each pick is its own block: the year and round, then Pick and Held by side by side with their "or" chains wrapping, then any protection or swap. A team's own picks and its traded-away picks are one line each
On a computer the draft picks table no longer runs off the right edge: notes and swaps wrap, and only the longest chains of teams do
The Stepien badge is a quiet lock instead of a yellow warning box
Coaching is on the team banner: under the next game, your own team's staff get a Coaching button that opens straight to their coaching settings, rotation and note to the streamer
Visitors no longer see a Coaching button on the Front Office tab. Only the team's own staff have Coaching

Player pages are redesigned to match the team pages: a team-colour header with the bio, this season's line and the next game (who he is projected to face, and a link to the preview), with the team's secondary mark behind it

One bar of tabs instead of two: Overview, Stats and Career, then 2K Ratings, Contract, History and Injuries. Overview opens on this season, with per-game numbers ranked across the NBN and his last 10 games
Season Stats, Advanced and Season Highs open with the newest season on top (each season's playoffs still under its regular season), and each team shows its logo and links to its page

The Stats and Career tables match the team page's: bigger type with room around each figure, a one-line note under every table, and playoff seasons marked PO. Season Stats is the per-game line, the made and attempted shots move to a new Shooting table, and win shares, BPM and VORP move from Advanced to a new Value table, so each fits without scrolling sideways. Most Games Together shows each teammate's headshot

Team pages are redesigned around the season: a team-colour header with the record, seed, streak and next game; the last ten results, the conference race, team leaders and both projected starting fives up top; then the roster, cap and picks, schedule, history and front office as tabs under it
Owners see their front office first on their own team page: deadlines coming up, what's waiting on them (offer sheets, team options, extension-eligible players) and one-click tools
On phones each roster row fits the screen: name, then position, OVR and age, then the contract and stat line
Old team-page links (#franchise, #schedule, #draft, #coaching) still land on the right section

The draft picks, schedule and season stats tables match the roster: team logos, one decimal throughout, months as bands in the schedule, and pick restrictions as badges. Historical Rosters is now Season Stats

The rest of the team page matches too: All-Time Top Players and Draft History show each player's headshot and name with one decimal throughout (All-Time shows the top 25, with the rest a click away); Rivalries name each opponent; Franchise Personnel lists Current and Former staff; win percentages read .439; and Best Team Season no longer counts a season still being played
Game times are gone from the team page
History has its own tabs: Franchise, Season Stats, All-Time, Records, Draft, Rivalries and Staff

Front Office: Coaching and IRL are separate tabs for a team's own staff, and the IRL feed opens on an overview of every player (status, last 5 and season averages, last game) with Game log and Injuries views and a date filter. On /nbnfl the feed gains the Injuries view and the date filter too
Free Agency opens in a couple of seconds instead of 20 or more: the player table no longer waits on the years-of-experience lookup, which also got much faster
Team pages and the rest of the site no longer slow down while someone has Free Agency open
The changelog page opens in half the time: it loads the latest 150 releases and has a Show older releases button for the rest
Fixed the homepage's ratings-changes card sometimes failing to load while new 2K ratings were arriving
Player names in Discord posts and inbox messages are spelled the way the site spells them: Jared McCain, RJ Barrett, Royce O'Neale (they read Jared Mccain, Rj Barrett, Royce Oneale)
Trade block: a player listed under an older spelling of his name is recognised as the same player
Calendar and streamer dashboard: the VOD link uses the site's play icon instead of an emoji
Old links to moved pages (/pdc, /schedule, /pickem, /trade-sim, /stats/highs/p and others) still land on the right page; the 22 placeholder pages that did it are gone
Team and Open Graph images are smaller to download, with no change to how they look
Discord: /roster and /lineups now start the same five as the team page for a team with no saved rotation. They could pick a different five before
Search (Ctrl+K) now finds league members: owners and GMs, past and present, each showing their current team and role, and linking to their member page
Homepage: the NBA Cup groups are now a second view of the Standings card (Standings | NBA Cup) instead of their own card
NBA Cup groups: the green Q1–Q4 tags are gone. Teams currently advancing are in bold, and the wild card is marked WC where there is room
Faster homepage: the Tonight graphic loads first, then the feed and the rest, instead of every card asking the server at once
Faster first paint on every page: stylesheets and fonts start downloading while the page is still arriving
The homepage no longer asks twice for the schedule, the stream status, the season's results or the version

Roster Settings: when 2K lists a player at a different position, your team page shows 2K's beside his, and edit mode lets you keep him as he is or take 2K's. You can choose at any time, including after a trade, which no longer resets his positions. Rulebook § 2.3 updated

Streamer dashboard: a new Roster Moves tab lists every trade, signing, release and waiver claim that still needs making in 2K, oldest first, with a Mark entered button. Contract-only moves like extensions aren't listed
Trades can now remove or lower a top-N protection that comes with fallback picks (like the 2029 SAS 1st), as well as plain protections

Trades can remove or lower a pick protection. In the trade builder, a team that protects a pick it owes can send that protection to the team owed the pick, for a 2nd or anything else, or keep only the top few picks of it
The office's transaction form can trade one team's share of a protected or swapped pick

Every submitted trade now has its own page. Inbox notices, #trc-alerts posts and the pending-trade note on your team page link straight to it, instead of to the TRC dashboard. Only the teams in the trade and the TRC can open it
Team schedules mark NBA Cup games with a Cup tag, and the calendar month view adds Cup to each Cup game
Homepage: on an NBA Cup night the Tonight poster says NBA Cup night once, instead of a Cup chip on every matchup card
Homepage: NBA Cup games are marked with a Cup chip on the matchup cards, beside the Stream chip
NBA Cup standings: a new NBA Cup tab on Standings shows every group, the wild-card race and the quarterfinals as they stand, on the NBA's tiebreak rules
Homepage: an NBA Cup card under the standings while the Cup is on
Stats committee: an Uploads done: parse now button starts the box score parse in the cloud, with a link to watch it run
Around the League: a player clearing or being claimed off waivers is tinted for the team that released him
Around the League: your team is called out again, more quietly. On a night of scores only your team's game is tinted, not the whole night, and a move naming your team is tinted

Homepage standings now match the rest of the app: the East/West and W–L/GB header row and the seed numbers use the app's display font, the play-in and lottery breaks are plain labelled lines instead of tiny dashed ones, and the top six seeds stand out in bold
Homepage: removed the blank band above the top of the page — the ticker on desktop and the menu bar on phones and tablets now sit where every other page's header does

Rotation editor: a player you pick up lifts off the table and floats above your finger, the spot he left is marked, and where he'll land is called out (a lit row with SWAP, or a bar with MOVE HERE). He settles into place when you let go
Rotation editor: swipe a player's minutes left or right to change them, with a big readout while you swipe. Tapping the number or the - and + buttons still works
Rotation and the rest of the Coaching tab restyled to match the Roster tab: display-face headings, OVR rating badges, and Starters / Bench / Inactive sections that show their minutes
Rotation: the minutes bar is now a Starters / Bench / Total strip that says whether you are balanced, short or over 240

Rotation editor: the sort buttons moved next to the Lineup / Details switch, the long help paragraph is now one line per view, and a player who can't start at his slot is marked with a red edge instead of a red block

Rotation editor: drag a player by the whole row (press and hold on a phone). Drop him on another player to swap the two, or between rows to slot him in; a label says where he will land, and the page scrolls on its own near the top and bottom
Rotation editor: split into Starters, Bench and Inactive, with a Lineup view (order and minutes) and a Details view (jersey numbers and secondary positions)
Rotation editor: new Sort bench button orders the bench by minutes, most first
Rotation editor: fits a phone screen now instead of zooming the page out
NBN Twitter: the compose box is now one line until you click into it — who you post as, the counter and Post appear then, and fold away again if you leave it empty
NBN Twitter: the new-identity fields (display name, handle, team) no longer show when you are posting as yourself
Highlight my team is off on the committee pages, Ratings Changes and Free Agency, where your own team shouldn't stand out
Homepage: once the Game of the Night's box score is in, the poster shows the final score in place of VS (linked to the box score), and each star's line from that game instead of his last 5
Homepage: the Tonight graphic loads sooner and no longer shows the old plain "11 games tonight" headline for a moment first

Streamer dashboard on a phone: the Coaching Settings list fits the screen. Each team is two lines (team and buttons, then its next game) and its card opens full width under it, instead of a table you had to scroll sideways
Streamer dashboard: saying what 2K showed for an overwritten player is a row of position buttons (PG SG SF PF C) for primary and secondary, instead of two dropdowns

Streamer dashboard: players whose new ratings went into 2K have their own section at the top of a team's card, Ratings Updated in 2K, showing what 2K should have for each, with Matches and Overwritten buttons

Streamer dashboard: a player flagged after a ratings update has his own save button, Good: 2K matches (or Set back in 2K: save, when 2K had something else), so he can be cleared on his own without Mark entered

Streamer dashboard: when the updates committee ticks a player Updated on Ratings Changes (his new ratings are in 2K), he is flagged on his team's card to check his positions weren't overwritten, and the next game's streamer is told. If 2K had something else, the streamer says what, sets it back, and marks it entered
Pages paint sooner: the shared stylesheets and fonts now download together instead of one after another
Homepage: Milestone Watch asks for every roster in one request instead of 30
Team pages: the header logo is a smaller file
Homepage Around the League: a night's final scores are no longer tinted for your team; the highlight there was too much
Highlight my team is now a choice in the account menu: your team's color, a color of your own (blue, sky, teal, violet, gold or orange), a star next to your team and players instead of a tint, or off

Highlight my team is easier to see and read: each team uses whichever of its colors stands out on your theme (Utah gold on the dark theme instead of navy, Golden State blue on the light one instead of yellow), and the small grey text on a highlighted row is brighter
Homepage Award Race: works like League Leaders. Pick an award (MVP, DPOY, ROY, 6MOY, MIP) to see its top three
Signed in with a team, your team and your players are now called out wherever they appear on the site: their row is tinted in your team's color, with a bar on its left edge
Account menu: a Highlight my team switch turns the callouts off and on

Homepage: hovering a row in Standings, Power Rankings, Around the League, Leaders, the award races, Milestones, Movers and On This Day shades the whole row, the way the Next Up scoreboard does, instead of underlining it. The name still turns blue
Homepage: your team card's schedule tiles and last night's three best players shade on hover too
Homepage Power Rankings: your own team's row is tinted in its team colour, so it no longer looks like a hovered row

Homepage: the Tonight card is now the Scoreboard, with a Last night | Tonight switch like Power Rankings has. Last night shows the latest night's final scores, each linking to its box score, with the game's video when it was streamed. It opens on Tonight
Homepage Power Rankings: a Model | Voted switch. The voted rankings are always one click away, dated, however old; the card opens on them for a month after a new edition and on the model after that
Homepage Power Rankings: the move badge is now a small outlined tag (+3, −3, NEW), centred on the row; no change is just a dash
Homepage Power Rankings: a team's move since last time is a small coloured badge (green up, red down, gold New) instead of a bare arrow

Homepage Power Rankings: when the voted rankings are more than a month old, the card ranks teams by the playoff-odds team rating instead, so it is always current. The voted edition still shows for a month after it is published

Homepage Power Rankings: each team shows its full name, record, streak, last 10 and title odds, with a bar in the team colour and your own team highlighted. The blurbs are gone; the full article still has them
Homepage Tonight card: every game lines up in the same columns, so the logos, records and @ sit straight down the card
Homepage Tonight card: on hover, the favourite’s record turns into its spread; once a game is played, the records become the scores and Final links the box score
Homepage Tonight card: the stream game is marked by its red edge alone; hover it to see who is streaming
Homepage Tonight card: opening a game shows the full team names (Boston Celtics at Toronto Raptors) above the starting fives
Homepage Tonight card: in a played game the winning team is in bold and the losing team is greyed out
Homepage Tonight card: back to one line per game (BOS 6–5 @ TOR 4–6). The spread still shows on hover, naming the favourite (CLE −14), and a played game shows its final on the same line
Homepage Tonight card: the stream game is marked by a red dot instead of an On stream label, still pinned to the top
Homepage Tonight card: the spread now appears only when you hover over a game (or tap it on a phone), beside the favourite, whose row lights up so it is clear which team it belongs to
Homepage Tonight card: the arrow at the side of each game shows only on hover
Homepage Tonight card: both teams in a game show the spread (−6.5 for the favourite, +6.5 for the underdog), so it is clear which team it belongs to
Homepage Tonight card: teams are named by city (Boston, Oklahoma City, LA Lakers) instead of their three-letter abbreviation
Homepage Tonight card redesigned: each game is a small scoreboard, away over home, with each team's record and the projected spread (e.g. −6.5 beside the favourite) instead of a tip time
Homepage Tonight card: the stream game is pinned to the top in red with an On stream label, in place of the Stream chip and name on a line of its own
Homepage Tonight card: played games show both scores, winner in bold, linking to the box score. Click a game for both starting fives; the game preview link is at their foot
Homepage Tonight graphic: the dots under the game cards now match the places the row can scroll to, so there are no extra dots at the end that go nowhere
Homepage Tonight graphic: Next on the last card goes back to the first, and Prev on the first goes to the last
Homepage Tonight graphic: the game cards no longer scroll by themselves

Homepage: the headline is now a Tonight graphic that changes every game day. A poster gives the night's game count and its game of the night (the stream game, else the biggest matchup) face to face: each team's hottest player over his last 5 games, in the teams' colours, with storylines scrolling underneath

Homepage: under it, a swipeable rail with a card for every game (both stars, records, a storyline or a milestone he's close to) and last night's three best players. It advances by itself; hover or touch to stop it, and it stays still with reduced motion on
Homepage: the Last night's best section is gone; its three players are the rail's first card
Discord: a Tonight card with the night's games and its game of the night is posted to #leaguetalk at 11am ET on every game day
Utah Jazz: the small team logo is white on the dark themes, so it no longer disappears against the page. It stays black on the light themes

Transaction Simulator: trades can include a pick swap. Under Pick swaps, a team gives another the right to swap one of its picks for theirs (same year and round); the other team ends with the better pick. Picks being traded can also be made top-N protected
Transactions: the office's trade form has the same Pick swaps rows. The old Swap column on pick rows is gone, since it couldn't record a normal two-team swap
Trades with a pick swap read as swap rights in the feed, the TRC dashboard, team pages and the transaction log
Years of experience are now NBN years: NBA years before 2020-21 plus each NBN season on a roster (rulebook § 3.1). The signing forms prefill this count instead of counting from the draft year

Homepage Injury Report: on a phone each player fits on one row. A red or gold bar marks Out or Hurt, and names, injuries and durations use short forms ("D. Peterson", "R Knee Tendinitis", "6-8w", "DTD")
Homepage team card: player faces in Matchup, and no faces on phones
Homepage team card: removed the arrows after Edit lineup, Full schedule and the alert bar

Homepage: your team card is redesigned as a team hub: a band in your team's colours with the record, conference rank and last and next game; the season numbers as blocks with each one's league rank; underlined tabs; and player headshots and OVR badges in Starting 5 and Injuries
Homepage: the team card no longer says All clear. When something needs you, it shows as a bar under the band
Ratings Changes: an Updated column. The new updates committee ticks each change once it is in the league 2K roster file, and anyone can filter to what is still to do
Roles and Committees: added the updates role and committee
Ratings Changes: attribute changes from the November 7 2K update showed as going from nothing to a value. They now show the real before and after
Homepage: a Market Movers card at the bottom of the side column, with the three biggest franchise share-price gains and drops on the last game day
Standings: removed the admin Post to Discord button
Members: a saved login no longer gets filled into the member search box, which emptied the table with "No members match these filters"
Hall of Fame: career stats now come before accolades
Hall of Fame: a # column numbers each row in the current sort; ties share a number

The Front Office Ledger is now Franchise Finances, and it opens on a new Market tab: a share price for every franchise, with market cap, P/E, daily movers and each team's price chart. Prices move on trades, signings, injuries and results, are built on the franchise's books, and can't be traded. Wall Street is unchanged
The books (franchise value history, each team's ledger, most valuable franchises, owners) are the Books tab, and arena naming rights have their own Arenas tab
The page keeps one team across its tabs: open a team's row on Market and its books are a click away

Season Stats: a new Per 36 view for players, with every counting stat and Game Score per 36 minutes, plus leader cards. Lines under 15 minutes a game sort after the rest so garbage-time minutes don't top the table
Minimum contracts signed after opening night are now prorated, as in the NBA: Year 1 pays the full minimum × regular-season days left ÷ days in the season. Rulebook § 3.12 spells it out
The office's minimum contract generator on /transactions and What If Mode's 1-yr Vet Min presets fill in the prorated figure, and the signing checks verify it instead of asking someone to confirm it
Homepage team card: a game played tonight now shows only as a result, not also as your next game
Stream Planner: a Hide saved days option. With it on, 7 days and 14 days show the next 7 or 14 days still to decide, skipping days whose stream is already set
Choose what the Planner prioritizes: Balanced, Team coverage, Rivalries, Team quality or Playoff race. The suggested picks and the scoring weights change to match
Game times are no longer shown in the Planner, and the calendar no longer shows a score under each pick
Stream Planner: a team on stream within a week can't be a day's suggested pick, so the same team (SAS) no longer tops day after day
Every open day starts with its suggested pick; swap or skip any day and the rest of the range re-ranks around your choices
Save all flags a whole range's streams in one go, with the list to confirm first; if any day was set in the meantime, nothing is saved
Days start collapsed to just what's streaming; expand a day for its ranked games
Calendar view: a month grid of each day's stream, with a day's games opening under its week
A side tally on desktop: plan summary, streams per team against the even share, and conference and division balance
Each game shows this season's meetings (and which were on stream) and both teams' last and next stream

Stream dashboard: a new Planner tab ranks each day's games for the stream by quality, closeness, owner and franchise rivalries, playoff stakes, star power, milestones and each team's fair share of streams, and shows why
Make stream on any ranked game flags it as that day's stream; a day with a flagged game is set, and a day with only a bought stream still gets its pick
Pick 7 days, 14 days, a month (the start date through the end of its month), or any range up to 31 days; a Streams by team table shows who is under or over the even share
Planner is the last tab, after Coaching Settings; on a phone the tab bar scrolls to keep the open tab in view

Stream vs Sim now compares about 60 team measures instead of player lines: shooting by type, where points come from, rebounding rates, fouls and free throws, rotations, big individual games and how games end
Each measure shows a gap bar and says whether the gap is clear, likely or could be noise, and the biggest real gaps sit in tiles at the top. Sort by biggest gap or show only real gaps

New Stream vs Sim page in the Stat Lab: how streamed games differ from quick-simmed ones (pace, shooting, fouls, how games end, rotations), each player's line both ways, and the list of streamed games. 26-27 is the first season with streams tracked.
A team at the roster limit can now name who it would release on an FA offer or a waiver claim. Nobody is released unless the offer or claim wins
The office's sign and offer sheet forms on /transactions take the same release list
Rulebook § 2.1: the rule against acquiring a player and releasing another at the same time is gone
NBN Twitter: a saved identity can now have its own profile picture. Pick the identity in the post box and use Add picture, or add one while creating a new identity

Declining a rookie-scale team option (a first-round pick's 3rd or 4th year) now always makes the player an unrestricted free agent, per rulebook § 6.1 and the NBA CBA. Since 0.15.9 these were wrongly tagged RFA-eligible. Tyler Smith, Bobi Klintman, Tyler Kolek and Cody Williams are corrected to UFA holds for 27-28

Rookie-scale team options open on July 1 of the season before the option year, so only next season's options (27-28 right now) can be exercised or declined. Sergio De Larrea's 28-29 option, accepted early, is back on his contract
Inbox redesign: messages that need you (trade block buttons) are pinned on top, the rest are grouped by day with a tag naming what each is about
Filter the inbox by view (Inbox, Unread, Needs you, Archived), by kind (free agency, trades, extensions...) or by searching
Messages are one line each; click one to expand it in place with the full text, its buttons, and Open / Mark unread / Archive
Mark messages unread, archive them, or select several and act on them at once; Mark all read only clears the kind you're filtered to
Turn off kinds of notification you don't want (messages with buttons always arrive)
The inbox refreshes itself, the unread badge in the sidebar updates as you read, and j/k/Enter/u/e/x keyboard shortcuts work
Team pages load faster: the Franchise, Draft History and All-Time Players tabs now fetch their data when first opened instead of holding up the roster
Team page roster: injured players show their injury badge, and players listed Out drop to the bottom of their group (the auto starting five skips them)
Team page draft picks: the year is shown once per group with a divider, the round is a pill (1st highlighted), and empty Protection / Swap / Frozen / Notes columns are hidden

Declining a team option no longer asks UFA or RFA: § 3.1 decides it from his experience, and the dialog says which. A player under 4 years (or finishing a first-round rookie deal) is RFA-eligible, so a qualifying offer can still make him an RFA
Team options left undecided at a deadline are now declined as RFA-eligible when § 3.1 says so, instead of always UFA

Declining a team option from the team page now asks whether his salary is above or below EAPS when the season has none set, suggesting an answer from this season's average salary, and shows the cap hold it leaves

Team pages: a team's GM and coach can now use the roster Moves menu (exercise or decline a team option, release, renounce, qualifying offers, two-way conversion, signing or stashing a draft pick). These were owner-only

Team Identity and the player archetype radar now show the current season from its first week, instead of waiting for 10 (team) or 20 (player) games. Early in a season the radar says how many games it is drawn from
Season Summary lists the season in progress, with its stat leaders so far
A team's current season no longer reads "Missed" for the playoffs before they start (Season History, timeline, standings, recaps). Needs the next stats build

Members: filter by role, team, position and active or former, search by name, and sort by any column. Click a role chip to see everyone else who has it. The filtered view is kept in the link, so it can be shared

A night's games stay "tonight" while the stream runs past midnight, or drops and restarts after it: Pick'em no longer opens on (or locks) the next day early, and the homepage slate, the stats committee worklist, game previews and the calendar stay on the night being played

Streamer dashboard: a team with no lineup on file gets a Record starters button on each game, so the five 2K actually started is still on record when an owner never sets one. Coaching Settings lists played games whose starters are unknown, with the game's streamer and VOD, to fill them in
Player pages: games started (GS) no longer shows a partial count as if it were complete. A season with games whose starters are unknown shows — until they're filled in
Stats Committee: new instructions for parsing box score screenshots with Claude Code, shown to the stats role. The Trigger a build button is gone; a build still runs after every box score commit

Advanced stats add Win Shares (offense, defense, per 48 minutes), Box Plus/Minus (offense and defense) and Value Over Replacement Player, on Season Stats and each player's Advanced table, with leader cards for all three. A team's Win Shares add up to about its wins: the points-per-win rate is set from NBN's own results, since margins here run wider than the NBA's

Season Stats has an Advanced view. Players get usage, assist, turnover, rebound, steal and block rates, plus three-point and free throw rates. Teams get pace, offensive and defensive rating per 100 possessions, net rating and the Four Factors. Hover a column header for what it means
Player pages have an Advanced table under Season Stats, with career lines

Team pages: Season History adds pace, offensive and defensive rating and net rating. The old Off Rtg and Def Rtg columns are renamed Off +/− and Def +/−, since they measure points against what each opponent had been allowing
Season Stats, All seasons: leader cards now need half a full season of games, so this season's first few games no longer top them
Homepage League Leaders: now the top three in each stat, with buttons to switch between points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and threes made.
Homepage on phones: the League Leaders card now sits with the other league cards, above Award Race, instead of at the very top of the page.

Homepage: a League Leaders card in the side column during the season, with this season's leader in points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and threes made. Each row opens the full list on /stats/seasons.

Rosters committee, Draft Picks: members with the rosters role can set a pick's protection bands from its card. The site previews what it will serve, checks that every slot in the round goes to exactly one team, and asks for the trade or ruling behind the change before applying it
The 2029 MIA and MIN 1sts now show the full swap: DAL gets the better pick, DET the worse, unless the worse lands 1-3, then MIN keeps it

Rosters committee, Draft Picks: ten picks now carry the protection bands the league sheet and the trade records agree on (2027 MIN 1st; 2027 DEN, LAL and MIN 2nds; 2028 ORL; 2029 ORL and SAC; 2030 ORL; 2031 GSW and TOR), so every team holding a share sees the pick on its page
Draft Picks: a pick where the sheet still names a team that has since traded its share away reads as Sheet is behind, not Teams disagree
Rosters committee, Draft Picks: committee tasks are grouped by what is being asked: missing trades first, then write-ups that contradict the records, then site fixes to confirm, then sheet-only fixes
Draft Picks reads more ways trades were written up (‘27, 28 LAC 2nd, an unnamed "2027 1st Round Pick", "Houston Receives"), which fills in most of the gaps in each pick's history

Rosters committee, Draft Picks: each trade in a pick's history now names who sent the pick. Where the write-up only says who received it, the sender is worked out (the other team in a two-team trade, or the team in the trade that held the pick) and shown in italics
Draft Picks marks a missing trade wherever a team trades a pick that no record shows it receiving

Rosters committee, Draft Picks: each flagged pick shows how it got where it is: every trade that names it (including trades only posted on Discord and missing from the transaction log), and every team tab on the league sheet that lists it as acquired
Draft Picks also checks the sheet's Acquired tables, so a split recorded only on another team's tab (the 2027 DEN 2nd) is flagged instead of reading as a clean match

Rosters committee, Draft Picks: a pick only counts as already reconciled when the sheet and the site name the same teams. Draft Picks lists site picks the sheet has no row for (WAS's 2033 picks), shows each split pick's teams and their share, names the team each side is missing, adds a team filter, and shows how long each committee task has been open

Wall Street 2 has a Market Summary like Wall Street: the top five risers and fallers over the last day, 7 days, 14 days or the season, each with a sparkline and, on the 1-day view, what happened to the team

Wall Street 2 no longer jumps to an empty day after midnight. Until a game is played on the new day it shows the last game day: the As of date, the Day column, the NBN 30 change and the daily moves all open on the day that was played

Roster Settings: when a player in the saved lineup is traded or released, his slot goes to a player not yet in the lineup instead of everyone below moving up a row, which could put a bench player out of position and block Save
Dropdowns inside pop-up forms open on top again. On the free-agency offer form they opened behind the form, so no exception, years or option could be picked and the offer could not be submitted.
Trades: any front-office member (owner, GM or coach) can now consent to or withdraw a trade for their team, not just the owner
Trade builder: coaches and GMs can now Submit to TRC for their own team. Only the team owner still has to consent
Wall Street 2: franchise revenue now grows with the salary cap after this season, so profits no longer shrink every year as payroll grows

Wall Street 2: from next season most national TV money becomes local TV that follows the team's market, and profit counts for more in the sale price, so big-market winners are worth much more than small-market strugglers (the gap between the top and bottom team goes from 3x to 5x)

Wall Street 2: the market mood is now based on real results (recent news, form over the last ten games, win and loss streaks, and last season's finals) instead of random swings, so a price barely moves on a day with no game and no news
Wall Street 2: each team's detail shows what its mood is made of, and the Beta column is gone
Wall Street 2: the sale price now counts profit as well as revenue, so payroll and tax reach a team's value
Wall Street 2: protected picks and swaps count by how often they actually convey, from simulated draft orders
Wall Street 2: player ageing is fit on NBN's own stats, and prices no longer drift up as the season goes by
NBN Twitter: signed-in members can post tweets from the homepage card, as themselves or under a made-up identity for scoops, and save an identity to use again
Every NBN Twitter post now also goes to the #twitter channel on Discord
Wall Street charts can compare two tickers: pick a team or index from Compare and both lines show as % change from the start of the range, lined up by date
Wall Street price charts open on the full history again, and the price axis fits each chart's own low and high, so the line keeps the shape it had before
Wall Street price charts: pick a range (10 games, 30 games, season, all), and the price, change and game result follow your finger or pointer. Replaces drag-to-zoom, which didn't work on a phone
Charts turn green or red with the move over the range, mark where it opened, shade the playoffs and label dates or seasons
Market Summary cards show a small price line, and scroll sideways on a phone instead of squeezing
Wall Street 2 (fair value) groups its columns under Franchise, Share, Ratios and This season
Opening a team now starts with a row of key figures (price, fair value, market cap, fair cap, revenue, profit, EPS, P/E, P/S, season range) instead of two lines of text
Daily moves notes read more plainly: "resale value +¥10M", "revenue outlook", "costs up", and "+0.3 projected wins" instead of "sale" and "proj W"
New Fair cap column next to Mkt cap: fair value × 30M shares, what the model says the whole franchise is worth
Wall Street 2 (fair value) fits on one screen: ledger value, fair ÷ ledger, PV profit and PV sale moved out of the table into each team's detail, and Beta shows only once it has ten days of history
Opening a team no longer cuts its details off at the right edge; the text wraps to the screen and stays in view when the table scrolls sideways
The team column stays in place while the table scrolls sideways on a phone, and a fade on the right edge shows there are more columns
The price chart fills the width, with short dates (Oct 20)
Title odds below 0.1% read "<0.1%" instead of 0.0%

Wall Street 2 (fair value) now counts a playoff edge. Front offices whose teams have beaten their regular season in past playoffs get a small boost in projected playoff series, which raises their title odds and value. Owners, GMs and coaches all count equally, and someone who changes teams takes their record along. Open a team to see its edge and who it comes from
The injury line on Wall Street 2 no longer reads "from 82.1 to 82.1" when an injury does not change a team's strength

Your team card on the homepage loads in one request instead of about a dozen when you come back signed in: the card and Starting 5 appear in about half a second, and the Matchup tab no longer loads anything of its own

Wall Street 2 (fair value) now plays out free agency in later seasons. Players whose teams let them go sign with whoever has the cap room or mid-level exception to pay them, so a team with space can add talent instead of filling the spot with a replacement player. Open a team to see who it is projected to sign and lose
Teams now keep their own free agents up to the second apron, and past it for anyone worth at least his cap hold, so a star is no longer projected to walk because of the first apron

Your team card on the homepage loads faster when you are signed in: it starts right away from the team you had last time, Starting 5 starts loading as soon as your team is known, and the slower cards at the bottom of the page (Milestone Watch, Award Race, Rookie Watch, Ratings Movers) now wait for it instead of loading first
Your team card's Starting 5 loads much faster: one request for the whole team instead of a full career game log per starter
Matchup fills the card: full team and player names, each starter's points per game, and more room. Phones keep abbreviations and last names
Each tab's link (Edit lineup, Game preview, Full schedule, Full report) now sits at the end of the tab bar, so no tab spends a row on it
Starting 5 no longer labels your own saved rotation; it only notes when the five is projected
In season the card only shows what needs you (like missing coaching settings) above the tabs. Notes like extension-eligible players stay on the team page and their own pages
The fair value page shows market cap as the first column after the team

During the season, your team card on the homepage now has tabs: Starting 5 (each starter's OVR, minutes, points, rebounds, assists, FG% and last five games, with injury tags and an Edit lineup link), Matchup (your five against your next opponent's), Schedule (your last 2 results and next 3 games, with back-to-backs marked), Injuries (your players on the report, with a count on the tab). Cap and roster lines are left off in season; the action chips (missing coaching settings, waivers, offers) show above the tabs only when there is something to do
The card's header line now shows your conference rank, streak, last 10, points for and against, point differential and offensive/defensive rating
The homepage standings show full team names when there is room, and switch to abbreviations on narrow screens
Fixed-odds bets now show American odds (like +300 or -150) next to each option's percentage

Standings ties are now broken the NBA way: head-to-head, then division winner, division record (only between teams in the same division), conference record, record against playoff teams, then point differential. Three-way ties start with division winner. A team that has not played a division game yet is no longer ranked as if it lost them all

Four past seeds changed as a result. 22-23: HOU is 6th and GSW 7th, matching HOU playing DAL in the first round. 24-25: UTA is 3rd and NOP 4th, matching the bracket. 20-21: LAC 7th and MIN 8th. 25-26: IND 8th and NYK 9th

Season Stats now shows offensive and defensive rebounds (per game and totals), personal fouls, true shooting % and effective field goal %, for players and teams. New leader cards for offensive rebounds and true shooting %

Wall Street 2 now has a market price. Fair value is what a franchise is worth and only moves when something happens. The price is what a share would trade at: it moves every day with the league's mood and the team's own, overreacts to news and gives it back, and has calm and wild stretches, like a real stock. The table shows both and how far apart they are, and each team's chart draws both lines
Fair value now counts a young core's and a top pick's rise two seasons past the projection, so a rebuilding team with young talent is worth more and an aging contender a little less

Wall Street 2 (fair value) reads like a stock page: market cap, price-to-sales, price-to-earnings and beta columns, the NBN 30 index (the average franchise price) at the top, and each team's season price range when you open it
Draft picks now count in fair value: a pick in the next two drafts adds its player, rated by where it is projected to land and improving with age. Open a team to see its first-round picks

Front Office Ledger: teams now have buzz, their form over the last ten games, judged by margin and by how good each opponent was. A hot streak raises ticket prices and merchandise straight away, a cold one cuts them, and a season of buzz moves next year's market. Every past season was recalculated
Wall Street 2 (fair value) counts buzz too: a hot streak pays this season and fades toward what the team's rating would sustain. Franchise values now span about 2.3× top to bottom

Front Office Ledger: teams now have a market. Everyone started 20-21 at 1.0×; each season, winning and playoff runs grow it and losing shrinks it. It scales ticket prices, merchandise and a new local TV and sponsors line, so franchise values spread wider: PHX is now worth about 2.2× CHA, up from 1.7×. Every past season was recalculated
Wall Street 2 (fair value) uses the same markets and projects them forward, so a playoff run moves a price further than before. Each team's season table shows its market

Wall Street 2 (fair value): each day's move says what happened, such as "W by 35 v IND", "Royce O'Neale hurt 2-4 weeks" or "CLE sign Harrison Ingram". The money breakdown only shows on a day when nothing happened to the team

Injuries now count in the price: a player who is out drops his team's strength for the games he is expected to miss, and a hurt one plays at his injured OVR. Open a team to see who is hurt and how many games it costs

Wall Street 2 (fair value): each day's move now reflects that day's games. Box scores posted after midnight or the next morning used to count on the following day, so some days showed no move and others showed two nights

Wall Street 2 (fair value): a day's move is now only what happened that day. Random noise from the simulation used to add up to 0.6% either way, so quiet days showed moves that weren't real. Every day since opening night was recalculated, and all prices shifted slightly
Wall Street 2 (fair value): a team's price chart shows only that team, so the scale fits its own moves
Wall Street 2 (fair value) now has every day since opening night (2026-10-20). The days before the model started were rebuilt from each day's box scores and are marked as rebuilt
Team pages show each player's Bird rights (Full, Early or Non-Bird) under his free-agent cap hold, with how it is known; estimates are marked with a ?
Player contract pages show the same Bird rights on each free-agent hold
Fixed: a re-signed player's next cap hold kept the Bird rights he signed with instead of the ones he will have by then. Dadiet's and Bruce Brown's 28-29 holds were corrected
Wall Street 2 (fair value): hover a column header for a one-line definition. The same list is under "How the price is worked out" for phones
Buying an arena's naming rights now posts to NBN Twitter on the homepage, from @NBNBizWire. If an admin pulls the name, the tweet goes too
You can buy things with NB¥ again: team themes (500), a custom avatar (500), and a name colour or status text (50)

Front Office Ledger: plain labels in place of the joke ones. "Paid to not employ him" is now "Dead money (released players)", and the rest read as Concessions and parking, Arena costs, Luxury tax, Share of other teams' luxury tax and Playoff ticket sales
Seasons with no payroll data now say so, instead of blaming a fire
Owners toggle is now Best owners / Worst owners
Front Office Ledger: the luxury tax now works like the NBA's, in brackets that get steeper the further a team is over the first apron
Teams that pay no tax now get an equal share of what the taxpayers paid
New revenue line for concessions (nachos, parking, foam fingers), which grows with the crowd, so a full arena earns more than its tickets
No two teams carry the same jersey-patch sponsor in the same season any more

Arena naming rights: bid NB¥ to name any team's arena, yours or a rival's, from the new table on Front Office Ledger. The next bid has to beat yours by 10%, and an outbid holder doesn't get their NB¥ back
Every box score now names the arena the game was played in
Browser tabs now lead with NBN, Discord-style: "NBN | Inbox" instead of "Inbox - NBN", so the site is easy to spot in a row of tabs. Shared links unfurl with the same title
League Office, About, Media and Games are now one link each in the sidebar instead of folding sections. Each opens its own page with a card for every page in it
On those pages (Rulebook, News, Perry, Proposals and the rest), the section name above the title links back to that page
Everything in them is still in search (Ctrl+K). Any of those pages you had pinned drops out of Pinned, since they no longer have a row of their own
Sidebar: the Teams basketball has thinner seams when you are on a team page, so it reads as a solid ball on dark themes
The filled star icon (Pinned in the sidebar) is a plain solid star now, without the small star inside
Sidebar: Games has a game controller icon instead of the basketball hoop
Sidebar: League Office has a briefcase icon instead of the gavel
The History trophy icon is a plain trophy now, without the star
Sidebar: a new Home entry at the top, above Teams, takes you to the homepage and fills in while you are there
Sidebar: the section you are on stands out more for NB¥ Corner, Front Office, Stats and Committees, whose icons now turn solid (a ¥ coin, a tile behind the arrows and bars, a filled building)
Sidebar: section icons are now outlines, and the section you are on fills in, so you can see where you are at a glance. In the collapsed sidebar the filled icon is the only marker
